messages:
jamie: Onboarding note — customer Sparrow sent a LoRA patch that merges cleanly but we're seeing increased token-level hallucinations on billing prompts. Need quick smoke pack run and root-cause hypothesis.
kevin: thanks. can you attach the eval pack you used and the merge diff?
maria: fyi I ran a fast lint on tokenization, no tokenizer id mismatch, but there is a subtle kvcache warm-start issue on longctx.
jamie: diff: patch applies to model/sparrow/adapter_lora_v2, small alpha=0.4 change. eval pack link: https://redwood.dev/evals/sparrow-smoke-2026-03-23
kevin: running quick smoke now with int4 quant profile q_config=fast-lowmem. will post results.
kevin: (run) ```bash
./run_eval.sh --model sparrow-lora-v2 --quant int4 --prompts smoke_billing.json --out /tmp/smoke.json
```
kevin: first pass: p95 latency +12%, token halluc rate up ~3.4% vs baseline, most failures on numeric amounts and currency symbols.
oliver: curious — did you warm the kvcache before eval? our serving runtimes need a couple warm queries for stable beam.
maria: i re-ran with explicit kvcache warmup (5 warm prompts) and switched to int8-quant fallback. halluc rate dropped to +0.8% vs baseline; suggests quantization interaction with cache.
jamie: good signal. can we isolate whether it's the LoRA weights or quantization? Suggest: run (A) float16 LoRA, (B) float16 base + int4 base (no lora), (C) float16 base + float16 lora, (D) int4 base + float16 lora.
kevin: queued jobs A-D on dedicated test pool. ETA ~25m. tagging @maria for evaluation criteria (golden prompts / threshold).
maria: golden set: 120 billing prompts, threshold: numeric exact-match >= 98.5%, fiscal-format detection F1 >= 0.97. Log granularity: include token-level alignments.
eval-bot: Job 87912 started on pool-dedicated-02. link: https://redwood.dev/jobs/87912
kevin: quick summary after runs: A(float16 LoRA): match 99.0% ok, B(int4 base no lora): 97.2% fail, C(float16 base+float16 lora): 99.1% ok, D(int4 base+float16 lora): 98.6% borderline.
oliver: that pattern points to quantized base weights causing the token-level misalignment; LoRA in float16 helps but int4 base still degrades.
jamie: proposed remediation: ship with int4 but enable kvcache warmup + prefix caching for billing route, and recommend float16 base for high-precision customers. Also add auto-fallback to float16 if numeric precision SLOs fail.
maria: agree. i'll draft a short notes doc for support and update the model catalog metadata: "sparrow-lora-v2: recommend base=float16 for billing-critical, kv_warmup=true".
kevin: I'll add a test in the smoketest harness to run the billing golden prompts on every merge with quant profile matrix.
jamie: thanks all — moving to patch rollout after change to recommended config. :thumbsup:
